facts.head: The Sun is a pretty average star.
facts.sub: many stars are far bigger and brighter

facts.head: The sunlight you see is 8 minutes old.
facts.sub: that's how long light takes to reach us

facts.head: The Sun holds almost all the mass in the solar system.
facts.sub: everything else shares the last 0.2%

facts.head: Over a million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
facts.sub: Earths would fit inside it

facts.head: One day the Sun will swell into a red giant.
facts.sub: it may grow past Earth's orbit

facts.head: The Moon has moonquakes.
facts.sub: recorded by Apollo seismometers

facts.head: We always see the same side of the Moon.
facts.sub: it spins once per orbit

facts.head: Footprints on the Moon could last millions of years.
facts.sub: nothing to wipe them away

facts.head: The Moon drifts away from Earth every year.
facts.sub: about as fast as your fingernails grow

facts.head: The Moon was probably made in a giant crash.
facts.sub: a Mars-sized world likely hit young Earth

facts.head: Mars is red because it's rusty.
facts.sub: rusty dust covers the planet

facts.head: A day on Mars is just a bit longer than ours.
facts.sub: a Martian day is called a sol

facts.head: Sunsets on Mars are blue.
facts.sub: fine dust scatters blue light near the Sun

facts.head: Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system.
facts.sub: almost 2.5 times Mount Everest

facts.head: One of Mars' moons is slowly falling toward it.
facts.sub: in ~50 million years Phobos may crash or become a ring

facts.head: Saturn is less dense than water.
facts.sub: water is 1.0, so in theory it would float

facts.head: Saturn's rings are mostly ice.
facts.sub: chunks of ice and a little rock

facts.head: A day on Saturn is under 11 hours.
facts.sub: it spins incredibly fast for its size

facts.head: Saturn has the most known moons of any planet.
facts.sub: and counting

facts.head: Saturn's rings are slowly disappearing.
facts.sub: ring material keeps raining onto the planet

facts.head: Jupiter is the biggest planet by far.
facts.sub: could fit inside it

facts.head: Jupiter has a storm wider than Earth.
facts.sub: the Great Red Spot has raged for centuries

facts.head: A day on Jupiter lasts under 10 hours.
facts.sub: the fastest spin of any planet

facts.head: Jupiter has rings too.
facts.sub: discovered by Voyager 1 in 1979

facts.head: Jupiter's moon Europa likely hides an ocean.
facts.sub: under a shell of ice

facts.head: Earth is the densest planet in the solar system.
facts.sub: thanks to its big iron core

facts.head: Earth is closest to the Sun in January.
facts.sub: seasons come from tilt, not distance

facts.head: Earth's core is about as hot as the Sun's surface.
facts.sub: the Sun's surface is ~5,500 °C

facts.head: Earth's days are slowly getting longer.
facts.sub: the Moon's tides are slowing our spin

facts.head: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy.
facts.sub: vs 100 to 400 billion stars

facts.head: Nothing can escape a black hole, not even light.
facts.sub: past the edge called the event horizon

facts.head: Black holes don't suck everything in.
facts.sub: swap the Sun for an equal-mass black hole and Earth keeps orbiting

facts.head: Time slows down near a black hole.
facts.sub: clocks tick slower close to it

facts.head: A giant black hole sits at the center of our galaxy.
facts.sub: its name is Sagittarius A*

facts.head: We have actually photographed black holes.
facts.sub: M87*, then our own Sagittarius A* in 2022

facts.head: Venus is the hottest planet.
facts.sub: hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the Sun

facts.head: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
facts.sub: 1 year = only 225 Earth days

facts.head: Venus spins backwards.
facts.sub: it turns the opposite way to most planets

facts.head: The air on Venus would crush you.
facts.sub: like being ~900 m deep in the ocean

facts.head: It rains acid on Venus, but it never lands.
facts.sub: it evaporates before reaching the ground

facts.head: Stars twinkle because of our air.
facts.sub: from space, they don't twinkle

facts.head: The starlight you see left long ago.
facts.sub: some naked-eye stars are 1,000+ light-years away

facts.head: There are probably more stars than grains of sand on Earth's beaches.
facts.sub: the universe is that big

facts.head: A sugar cube of neutron star weighs about a billion tons.
facts.sub: about as heavy as a mountain

facts.head: Many stars come in pairs.
facts.sub: have a partner star
